traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Styracaceae: leaves alternate; leaves simple; margins entire, crenate, serrate or dentate; veins pinnate; stipules absent; plants usually hermaphrodite, rarely polygamous; ovary superior, half inferior or inferior; floral cup present or absent; stems woody; flowers in cymes, in racemes or in panicles, rarely solitary; flowers actinomorphic; perianth sepals and petals; fruit capsule or samara, rarely drupe; stamens (5-) 8 to 10 (-20); carpels (2-) 3 to 5. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.fruit_type.note: Wikipedia Styracaceae (read 2026-10-17; 12 genera, ~160 spp, Styrax about 130 of them): fruit mostly a dry capsule, sometimes winged, less often a fleshy drupe. Flora of Taiwan Styrax (read 2026-10-17): fruit globose, opening by three valves or irregularly. Winged fruits are confined to the small genera (Halesia, Pterostyrax and kin, under 20 spp).

traits.inflorescence.note: Flora of Taiwan Styrax (read 2026-10-17): flowers in axillary or terminal racemes, simple or branched (branched ones read as panicles). Styrax is about 130 of ~160 species in the family (Wikipedia Styracaceae, read the same day), so its racemes decide.

traits.ovary_position.note: Flora of Taiwan Styrax (read 2026-10-17): calyx cup free from the ovary or only slightly joined to it, so the ovary sits essentially superior in Styrax, about 130 of ~160 family species (Wikipedia Styracaceae). The family account there allows superior or inferior; the inferior and half-inferior ovaries belong to the dozen small genera.
